restoration_contract.original_intent: Restore the raw Git blob using git show RESTORE_COMMIT:COMPLETE_PATH into a fresh scratch file; verify byte count and git hash-object equal the recorded Git blob. Keep it outside the active topic until a consumer actually needs it. This operation is file recovery, not a scientific replay.
restoration_contract.large_blob_reading: Do not retrieve these >=100KB files through an integrated full-text reader. Use the existing Git-backed file recovery route when an execution environment is available. The current review performed metadata-only checks for them.
restoration_contract.sha256: The candidate SHA256 is intentionally null. Compute it only from the actually restored raw bytes when needed; do not hash a summary or reconstructed JSON and call it the old file.
restoration_contract.warm_and_status: Recover the actual warm and compressed status at the per-run restore commits. Check compressed file hashes; decompress status once and check its original uncompressed byte count and SHA256. Do not parse/re-serialize status to satisfy the original guard.
restoration_contract.source_and_parameters: Retain all complete source files, original requests, complete non-files manifest contexts, original configuration, result notes, restoration receipts and the immutable workflow references in this receipt. No reduction of variables, rows, tolerances or budgets is authorized.
restoration_contract.replay: A new scientific rerun, if later requested, must execute only through public Actions with the complete original source/parameter/input closure. No such rerun is necessary to recover the original audit bytes, and no claim is made that a numerical rerun reproduces historical output bytes.
restoration_contract.history: Keep the actual finite successes, nearest rejection cases and unresolved scientific scope. A one-step warm acceptance and finite directional test do not establish the remaining full closed BVP or continuous geometric goal.
